title: Count Magical Substring Pairs II
statement: The task is to count triplets i ≤ j < k where s[i..j] and s[j+1..k] have equally many distinct letters, for a lowercase string with n up to 10^5. Fixing the split point j, the answer sums over d ≤ 26 the substrings ending at j with exactly d distinct letters times those starting at j+1, each count being at-most-d minus at-most-(d−1) from sliding windows (two pointers).
